observation_summary: The NumericEntityUnescaper failed to correctly unescape numeric entities representing supplementary characters (code points > 0xFFFF), resulting in incorrect character output.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the logic for writing the unescaped character to the output stream. Specifically, it adds a conditional check to handle supplementary characters (code points > 0xFFFF) by converting them into a pair of UTF-16 surrogate characters using Character.toChars(), rather than attempting to write the raw integer value directly. This is a procedural correction to the unescaping algorithm to correctly handle multi-char UTF-16 representations.
evidence_used: The fix diff shows an added conditional block: if(entityValue > 0xFFFF) { char[] chrs = Character.toChars(entityValue); ... }
The failing test case expected a supplementary character (\uD803\uDC22) but received an incorrect character.
The bug report mentions that supplementary characters require more than 1 Java char to be encoded.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a conditional check (if entityValue > 0xFFFF), the primary purpose is to implement the correct transformation logic (converting to surrogate pairs) for that specific case, which is an algorithmic requirement for handling supplementary characters.
The fix is not about assigning a wrong value or initializing a variable, but about changing the procedural logic of how the output is written.
